newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar closes firmer in light trading.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar closes firmer in light trading.

text.p: * The Canadian dollar closed firmer on Monday at C$1.3443 (US$0.7439) from Friday's close at C$1.3470 (US$0.7423) in light trading, dealers said.
* They said the National Association of Purchasing Management index released in the United States this morning boosted Canadian bonds, which helped the currency.
A Reuters poll of Wall Street economists had expected the indicator to post a 53.0 reading in January.
The news helped push Canada's benchmark 30-year bond up C$0.67 to C$109.85 to yield 7.162 percent.

The currency rallied on the numbers until midday and drifted in the afternoon despite statements from Canadian Finance Minister Paul Martin that the federal budget on February 18 would show the government well ahead of its budget targets.
Martin also said he saw the possibility of "very targeted" tax cuts.
Traders said market players were not anxious ahead of Tuesday's U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, since the meeting was expected to leave U.S. interest rates unchanged.
Instead, all eyes were on Friday's employment reports expected in the United States and Canada, dealers said.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar edged up to 1.2178 marks from Friday's close of 1.2154 marks and rose to 90.42 yen from 90.03 yen.
